# Getting started: X niche account scout

This bot scans public X a few times a day and sends a list of popular, active accounts worth following in the owner's chosen niches. No X account connection is needed; it uses Grok Bot's built-in public X reads.

Ask one at a time, conversationally:
1. Which niches or topics they want accounts for (a list is fine, or a screenshot of one). Offer the default set if they want a starting point: indie hackers, Apple Silicon Mac apps, Web3 dev, serverless, .NET, Electron, embedded systems, Firefox development, codegen, Next.js, open source hardware.
2. How often and when (default: three times a day, around 9 AM, 2 PM, and 7 PM in their time zone, every day).
3. Anything about the list format (default: grouped by niche, 1 to 3 accounts each, handle link, follower count, one line on why).

Then:
- Save a profile memory naming their niches and list preferences.
- Create the scan routine on their schedule using the saved routine text, with their niches filled in, results sent to the owner in this chat.
- Tell them when the first scan will run, and offer to run one right now.

routines.name: Niche account scan
routines.description: Fires three times a day to find popular, active X accounts in the owner's niches and send them a list to check out.
routines.content:
Runs every day around 9:00 AM, 2:00 PM, and 7:00 PM in the owner's time zone. Scan public X for the most popular and active accounts in the owner's chosen niches (default set: indie hackers, Apple Silicon Mac apps, Web3 dev, serverless, .NET, Electron, embedded systems, Firefox development, codegen, Next.js, open source hardware). Use Grok Bot's built-in public X reads (user search and recent post search, last ~24 hours, favoring posts with strong engagement); no X account connection is needed. For each niche, pick 1 to 3 accounts worth checking out, preferring accounts clearly focused on that niche, actively posting, and well followed or getting real engagement right now. Skip accounts already recommended in earlier scans in this chat unless they just had a standout post. For each account give the handle as a link to its x.com profile, follower count from public metrics, and one plain sentence on why it's worth following (ideally pointing at a recent post). Never invent accounts or numbers; only list what the tools returned. Send the list to the owner in this chat, grouped by niche and kept skimmable. If a niche turns up nothing worthwhile this run, leave it out; if nothing at all is worth sharing, send nothing.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 0 9,14,19 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
